stick.gimbal.name: Stick (roll / pitch)
stick.gimbal.note: force-sensing stem under the grip connector (roll X / pitch Y)

unplaced.stick.axis.twist: the user guide documents no twist sensor (only roll/pitch; SSF firmware yaw = side force with pinky held); no grip on this photo

source: JoyPro curated on the maker's photo (2026-10-11), the FSSB R3L "Lighting" force-sensing base alone (no grip) seen from the front, grip connector on top
mappingSource: FSSB-R3 User Guide (https://www.realsimulator.com/download/FSSB-R3_User_Guide.pdf) p.32/37/94: Roll = X axis, Pitch = Y axis; p.78-84: the SSF firmware adds Yaw by swapping the X force to Yaw while the pinky is held; catalog realsimulator.json also cites https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3221478/Realsimulator-Fssb-R3-Lighting.html
note: The base has no moving gimbal (force sensing); the roll/pitch marker sits on the sensing stem under the grip connector. Catalog discrepancy: the catalog lists a twist axis (JOY_RZ); the user guide documents only Roll (X) and Pitch (Y), plus a Yaw axis in the SSF firmware made from the side force while the pinky is held, not a grip twist. The twist part is therefore not placed.
